notes: Real plate: baked/blackened salmon, white rice, roasted asparagus, dinner roll — well-lit, single plate, foods clearly visible; verify must stay quiet. FOOD_DB has no asparagus or dinner-roll entries, so green-beans (closest vegetable) and bread-whole-wheat (closest starch) stand in as nutritional proxies. Servings reverse-engineered to roughly match the app's own prior real analysis of this exact meal (46g protein / 62g carbs / 22g fat / 620 kcal) — reconstructs to ~47.5p/66c/22f/665kcal, fat exact. SOURCE NOTE: this file is an app screenshot (has status bar + confirm-screen UI chrome baked into the pixels), not a clean raw camera capture — replace with a real un-cropped device photo when the team adds one; it still exercises the full harness end-to-end.

Real photo: staff lunch tray, 4 meatballs in marinara over rice, mashed potato and sauteed pepper/onion sides. Well-lit, distinct compartments; verify must stay quiet. FOOD_DB has no meatball, mashed-potato, or onion entries: ground-beef-90 stands in for the meatballs (undercounts the sauce and any egg/breadcrumb binder), white-potato for the mashed potato (a whole-potato serving, not truly equivalent to a mashed portion), and bell-pepper for the pepper/onion side (the onion itself has no DB entry at all and is fully excluded from ground truth). Expect the reconstructed macro truth to run LOW, especially fat/carbs, independent of which model reads the photo.

Real photo: to-go container, sliced braised/roasted beef in its own jus, roasted potato wedges, green beans. Well-lit, single well-separated compartment, foods clearly visible; verify must stay quiet. FOOD_DB has no braised-beef entry, so sirloin-steak stands in (closest protein; the real dish is fattier/moister with pan jus, so this proxy likely undercounts fat and total kcal a bit).

Real photo: plated dinner, saucy chicken chunks, sliced beef in gravy, cooked collard greens, white rice. Well-lit, foods distinct; verify must stay quiet. FOOD_DB has no collard-greens entry — spinach (only 'greens'-aliased proxy) stands in, but real cooked collards (usually simmered with fat/pork) run FAR higher in kcal/fat per cup than raw spinach (7 kcal/cup vs. a real serving likely 60-100+ kcal). This proxy will make the collard-greens component read as nutritionally almost free no matter what any model reports — a FOOD_DB coverage gap, not a model error. Treat this case's kcal/fat ground truth as a floor, not a true value.

Real photo: scrambled eggs, 3 bacon strips, 2 breakfast-sausage links, cheddar grits, side of grapes. Well-lit, foods clearly visible; verify must stay quiet. FOOD_DB HAS NO BACON, SAUSAGE, OR GRITS ENTRY AT ALL — bacon and sausage are fully excluded from expectedFoods (not proxied to anything; there is no reasonable stand-in), and oats (the only porridge-category item) proxies for the grits despite being a different grain. This is the most FOOD_DB-limited case in the set: expect ground-truth kcal/protein/fat to run far below any real read, for every model, because roughly half the plate's calories (bacon + sausage) have no ground-truth representation at all. A model that reports bacon/sausage honestly will look artificially WORSE on macro error here than one that hallucinates less food.
